¿Cómo se calcula la solubilidad a partir: How do you calculate solubility from Ksp?
Para una sal AₐB_b, Kps = aᵃ·bᵇ·s^(a+b),: For a salt AₐB_b, Ksp = aᵃ·bᵇ·s^(a+b), so s = (Ksp/(aᵃ·bᵇ))^(1/(a+b)). For AgCl (Ksp = 1.8·10⁻¹⁰), s = √(1.8·10⁻¹⁰) ≈ 1.3·10⁻⁵ mol/L; for Ca(OH)₂ (Ksp = 5.5·10⁻⁶), Ksp = 4s³ and s ≈ 0.011 mol/L.
¿Cómo se calcula el Kps a partir de la s: How do you calculate Ksp from solubility?
Se pasa la solubilidad a mol/L (g/L entr: Convert the solubility to mol/L (g/L divided by the molar mass), multiply by the coefficients to get the concentration of each ion and substitute into Ksp = [A]ᵃ[B]ᵇ. For Ag₂CrO₄ with s = 6.5·10⁻⁵ M: [Ag⁺] = 1.3·10⁻⁴ M, [CrO₄²⁻] = 6.5·10⁻⁵ M and Ksp = 4s³ ≈ 1.1·10⁻¹².
Si la disolución ya contiene uno de los: If the solution already contains one of the ions of the salt, the salt dissolves less. AgCl in 0.10 M NaCl satisfies s(s + 0.10) = 1.8·10⁻¹⁰, giving s ≈ 1.8·10⁻⁹ mol/L: about 7,400 times less soluble than in pure water.
¿Cómo saber si una sal precipita al mezc: How do you know whether a salt precipitates when two solutions are mixed?
Se calculan las concentraciones tras mez: The concentrations after mixing (they are diluted) and the ionic product Q = [A]ᵃ[B]ᵇ are calculated and compared with Ksp: if Q > Ksp it precipitates, and if Q < Ksp it does not. With 50 mL of 0.01 M Pb²⁺ and 50 mL of 0.01 M I⁻, Q = 0.005·0.005² = 1.25·10⁻⁷, greater than the Ksp of PbI₂ (9.8·10⁻⁹), and it precipitates.

La sal es A<sub>a</sub>B<sub>b</sub>: a: The salt is A<sub>a</sub>B<sub>b</sub>: a cations and b anions per formula unit (Ag₂CrO₄: 2 and 1). With the solubility in g/L the molar mass is needed, which comes from the formula if you write it.
Escribe a y b (cationes y aniones por fó: Enter a and b (cations and anions per formula unit) and the Ksp, or choose an example salt (values from commonly used tables at 25 °C; use those of your book if they differ). The formula is optional: it gives the g/L.
Escribe la concentración del ion que ya: Enter the concentration of the ion already in the solution (the one the salt also gives): for example, 0.10 M Cl⁻ if there is 0.10 M NaCl and the salt is AgCl.
Concentración de cada ion en su disoluci: Concentration of each ion in its solution, before mixing (that of the ion, not of the salt: in 0.01 M Pb(NO₃)₂, Pb²⁺ is 0.01 M). With the molar mass or the formula the mass of precipitate is also calculated.
La sal con un anión básico (OH⁻, CO₃²⁻,: A salt with a basic anion (OH⁻, CO₃²⁻, F⁻, CrO₄²⁻, PO₄³⁻…) dissolves more as the pH falls. For a hydroxide the pH fixes [OH⁻]; for the other salts enter the pKa of the conjugate acid of the anion, from lowest to highest (CO₃²⁻: 6.35 ; 10.33). The pH is assumed to be held by a buffer.
El catión forma complejos con un ligando: The cation forms complexes with a ligand (NH₃, S₂O₃²⁻, OH⁻…) and the salt dissolves more. Enter the initial concentration of the ligand and the log β of formation of the complexes, one by one: “3.32 ; 7.23” are log β₁ and log β₂ of Ag(NH₃)₂⁺ (β₂ = β₁·K₂). The ligand that is consumed is taken into account.
Dos sales con un ion que se va añadiendo: Two salts with an ion that is gradually added (Ag⁺ to a mixture of Cl⁻ and CrO₄²⁻). The concentration is that of the other ion of each salt, before starting to add.
Base conjugada de un ácido débil: Conjugate base of a weak acid
de menor a mayor, separados por «;»: from lowest to highest, separated by “;”
Un catión (Ag⁺ a Cl⁻ y CrO₄²⁻): A cation (Ag⁺ to Cl⁻ and CrO₄²⁻)
Un anión (I⁻ a Pb²⁺ y Ba²⁺): An anion (I⁻ to Pb²⁺ and Ba²⁺)
Diagrama logarítmico: la recta es el lím: Logarithmic diagram: the line is the saturation limit ([A]^a·[B]^b = Ksp). Above it there is supersaturation and it precipitates; below it, the solution can take more salt.
El punto está sobre la recta de saturaci: The point is on the saturation line, with the common ion already present: the more common ion, the less salt dissolves.
Solubilidad de la sal en función del pH: Solubility of the salt as a function of pH (logarithmic scale). The black point is the pH you entered; the dotted line, the solubility without taking the protonation of the anion into account.
Solubilidad de la sal en función de la c: Solubility of the salt as a function of the initial ligand concentration (logarithmic scale). The black point is the concentration you entered; the dotted line, the solubility in pure water.
El punto naranja es la mezcla recién hec: The orange point is the freshly made mixture (above the line, it precipitates; below, it does not). If it precipitates, the black point is the final equilibrium on the line.
Cada recta es una sal: [${sol.cat ? 'B': Each line is a salt: [${sol.cat ? 'B' : 'A'}] versus [${sol.cat ? 'A' : 'B'}] at saturation. The orange points mark where each one starts to precipitate; the black one, what remains of the first when the second starts.
